I really think that DataMelt scientific computational environment is among solid alternative's of Mathematica. First, it's free. Second, it's Java and runs on Linux, Mac and Windows. It has everything that Mathematica has, namely:

• Function plotting in 2D and 3D Histogramming in 2D and 3D Data
• analysis Statistical packages (regression, non-linear fits)
• Symbolic computations with a number of Java engines
• Calculations with physics/measurements units
• Very strong IO (some based on Java serialisation)
• Very good IDE with Help assist
• Very detailed manual about 300 examples and a book
• A number of languages are supported (Python, Groovy, Java, Ruby) You can mix programming with high-level math calculations

World Down Syndrome Day: Celebrating Progress and Unleashing Unlimited Potential
Every day, people around the world demonstrate that nothing is impossible. Athletes, musicians, professionals, parents, children, and others constantly break barriers, defy expectations, and achieve remarkable feats.
Individuals with Down syndrome are no different; March 21st is World Down Syndrome Day (WDSD) — a day that holds significant meaning for individuals with Down syndrome, their families, and advocates around the world. WDSD is a day to celebrate the unlimited potential and accomplishments of individuals with Down syndrome while also acknowledging the societal hurdles they still face.
At GiGi’s Playhouse, we love WDSD; it’s a day that allows us to share with the world how incredible our participants are!
But before we dive into the importance of WDSD, we need to explain why it exists!
World Down Syndrome Day Origins
World Down Syndrome Day was first observed by various countries in 2006, and in 2012, the United Nations officially recognized it. The date of March 21st is significant, as it symbolizes the triplication (trisomy) of the 21st chromosome — the cause of Down syndrome.
Why is it important?
While WDSD is a day of celebration, and at GiGi’s Playhouse, we celebrate accordingly, it’s also so much more than that. WDSD shows how far we’ve come as a society.
In the not-so-distant past, individuals with Down syndrome were often met with limited expectations. Many were denied opportunities to learn, grow, or pursue their passions. For generations, individuals with Down syndrome were placed in segregated environments, excluded from mainstream education, and often seen through a lens of limitation. The prevailing belief was that their diagnosis defined them — that their potential was capped simply because of an extra chromosome.
But things have changed.
While there is still work to be done — the Down syndrome community continues to face challenges like high unemployment rates and ongoing discrimination — significant progress has been made.
As society’s understanding of Down syndrome has evolved, so have expectations. People are beginning to realize that individuals with Down syndrome are capable of so much. As expectations have changed, so have the achievements of individuals with Down syndrome.
Today, individuals with Down syndrome attend college, become entrepreneurs, participate in sports, thrive in the arts, and contribute in countless ways to their communities.
The difference? Belief.
Belief in their potential. The belief that, like anyone, they can achieve great things when given the proper support, opportunities, and encouragement.
At GiGi’s Playhouse, belief is at the heart of everything we do. We wholeheartedly believe in the unlimited potential of individuals with Down syndrome.
We know they face specific obstacles—low muscle tone, difficulty with speech, developmental delays—but our FREE purposeful and progressive programs help them gain confidence, overcome these obstacles, and accomplish their dreams.
But we’re affecting more than individuals with Down syndrome and their families through our unwavering belief and free programming. Our network of Playhouses help entire communities realize the unlimited potential that individuals with Down syndrome have. This realization then sparks societal expectations to change and allows individuals with Down syndrome to continue to break barriers and achieve their dreams.
This World Down Syndrome Day — and every day — GiGi’s Playhouse is proud to showcase the incredible capabilities and potential of individuals with Down syndrome.
It’s through highlighting the achievements, resilience, and potential of the Down syndrome community that we can shift perceptions and ultimately transform the world!

Today, you must compete for student attention. You compete with hundreds of channels available through cable and satellite television. Our phones and tablets stream most of them too! This is not to mention computer games, social media, and everything else available through the internet and cyberspace.
Our kids are overstimulated and our teachers overwhelmed as they endeavor to get their students interested and involved in the curricula. Paradoxically, it is our own lessons that teach students when they can be off-task and when they can minimally participate in class! The notion that fairness and that everyone must participate the very same way often create habits and gaps in student attention in the classroom.
The good news is that promoting attention and interest is immediately doable!
Differentiated Instruction Benefits for Students
- Students in Differentiated Instruction classrooms enjoy a number of advantages over those in traditional “one-size fits all” approach settings. Students are able to be active participants in their own learning.
- The curriculum is no longer pointed to the middle of the group but available and interactive to all students. Those students that found a traditional classroom lesson too difficult or something they had already learned which led to feeling of being “bored” or “not engaged” are now excited about their learning.
- Students receive the content and curriculum in ways that ensure they are engaged. This engagement allows students to connect and learn the content at a deep level of understanding.
